subject: Axios Pro Rata: Anthropic's IPO path

Plus, bank merger murmors | Wednesday, September 30, 2026

PRESENTED BY J.P. MORGAN
 
Axios Pro Rata
By Dan Primack · Sep 30, 2026
 
 
Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images
 

Anthropic already was going to be the defining IPO story for Q4, but now takes on greater significance as other companies postpone or scrap their offerings due to "market conditions."

The big question: Will the Claude maker go public before Thanksgiving, or follow the crowd (and OpenAI) into the "wait 'til next year" wilderness?

Behind the scenes: I'm not hearing anything different than earlier in the month, but it's still worth a quick look at the debate.

The bull case: The AI industry is weathering the PR storm better than it could have hoped, and Anthropic really needs the money at a time when it could have the capital-markets stage to itself.

  • Stock prices continue to rise, despite "alignment" becoming a kitchen-table term and increased talk of slowing new model releases.
  • SpaceX, which is both an Anthropic rival and vendor, is up for the month. So are Nvidia, Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft, etc. Not huge gains, but even treading water is notable in a tsunami.
  • Speaking of SpaceX, a quick reminder that it first shocked everyone with massive losses and then went out to raise the largest IPO ever.

Also: Anthropic could keep tapping the private markets — like OpenAI reportedly plans to do — but more structure often means more problems. An IPO creates a public currency and puts pressure on its key competitor. Plus, Anthropic sincerely believes that safety is enhanced via the transparency of being a public company.

  • Finally, some of Anthropic's regulatory risk was diluted by yesterday's dog-and-pony show at the White House. It might be a small window. Get public while the politics are palatable.

The bear case: Wall Street might choke on the losses, and you only get one chance to make a first impression.

  • Reuters recently reported that Anthropic booked $42 billion of red ink in 2025, which managed to make SpaceX look like a bit player.
  • Yes, most of that is tied to stock-related accounting charges, but there's some thought that the leak was designed to prepare everyone's stomach for even more galling 2026 losses.

Also: Anthropic leadership has mission muddle that other frontier labs don't seem to share, at least not as loudly. The company's bankers must ensure that CEO Dario Amodei can clean that up before the roadshow, let alone earnings calls.

  • Then there's the frantic game of model hopscotch between Anthropic and OpenAI. At this very moment, Anthropic seems to be slightly behind.
  • Finally, the broader trend of IPO postponements could give Anthropic some cover for pacing its financial frontier — particularly if it believes the numbers could look better if it waits, and that the $2 trillion valuation was too aggressive.

The bottom line: Anthropic needs to do a financing event. The only question is what kind.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

Piper Sandler (NYSE: PIPR) is in talks to buy advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners (Nasdaq: PWP), per the WSJ.

Why it's the BFD: Bank consolidation is nothing new — Piper Sandler itself is the result of a 2020 merger — but this reflects how many boutique advisories are struggling to defend their niches.

By the numbers: Piper Sandler shares fell nearly 10% yesterday on the news, giving it a $4.6 billion market cap.

  • Perella Weinberg shares surged nearly 12%, pushing its market cap above $1.5 billion.

The bottom line: "Perella Weinberg did a series of its own deals over the years. Earlier this year, it struck a deal for the U.K.-based advisory firm Gleacher Shacklock, and last year it agreed to acquire secondary advisory firm Devon Park Advisors. The bank previously bought the energy-focused boutique bank Tudor Pickering Holt in 2016." — Lauren Thomas & AnnaMaria Andriotis, WSJ
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

• Hertha Metals, a Conroe, Texas-based green steel producer, raised $134m in Series A funding. Khosla Ventures and Doerr Capital led the round, which included $65m from the U.S. government. Other backers include CEV, Pear Ventures, Gates Frontier, Niterra SUISO no MORI Fund, Toyota Ventures, and Siemens Financial Services. axios.link/3VXP7Eo

• Jeeves, an Orlando, Fla.-based stablecoin-native banking platform for enterprises, raised $110m. CoinFund led, joined by AllianceBernstein, Vista Equity Partners, Coinbase Ventures, a16z, and YC. axios.link/4ymo3x3

• Efficient Computer, a Pittsburgh-based developer of energy-efficient processors, raised more than $97m in Series B funding at a $650m valuation. TQ Ventures led, joined by Eclipse, Union Square Ventures, Giant Ventures, Triatomic Capital, TO Capital, TF Capital, Mana Ventures, Toyota Ventures, Overmatch, and Borderless. axios.link/4dbPgdt

• Reco, an Altamonte Springs, Fla.-based AI security startup, raised $55m from AT&T Ventures, Forestay, and Quadrille Capital. axios.link/4AFfVsZ

• Metaview, a London-based agentic recruiting platform, raised $60m in Series C funding, per Axios Pro. Insight Partners led, joined by GV, Intrepid Growth Partners, Seedcamp, Vertex, Plural, and Garuda Ventures. axios.link/4jwjA6n

🚑 Aptadit Therapeutics, an Italian developer of RNA inhibitors for genetic diseases, raised $45m in seed funding. 4BIO Capital led, joined by Extend, CDP Venture Capital, XGEN Venture, and CE-Ventures. axios.link/4hT7HpR

• Miter, an SF-based construction workforce management platform, raised $40m in Series B funding, per Axios Pro. Battery Ventures led, joined by insiders Bessemer Venture Partners and Coatue. axios.link/4rHQzqD

• HyperGuest, an Israeli travel tech startup, raised $25m from Apax Mid-Market Israel. axios.link/4iXdzzy

• Proximal, an SF-based coding startup, raised $15m in seed funding led by General Catalyst at a $300m valuation, per the Information. axios.link/4hnapUn

• Kanu AI, a Seattle-based developer of specialized software for enterprises, raised $11.7m in seed funding, per Axios Pro. Trilogy Equity Partners led, joined by a16z, BMW i Ventures, and Accel. axios.link/3TxzLFR

• Inbolt, a French industrial robotics vision startup, raised €11m. Shift4Good led, joined by Bridges Climate Transition Partners, BNP Paribas Développement, and Ora Global. axios.link/46TcqBH

• Rayon, a provider of drawing software for interior designers, raised €10m in Series A funding. Partech led, joined by insiders Northzone, Foundamental, and Seedcamp. axios.link/4rFkSxV

• Zenithon, a U.K. developer of world models for extreme physics, raised $10m from Backed, Lunar, Seraphim, MMC, and SOSV. axios.link/46TcC3T

• Beltic, an SF-based agent verification platform, raised $8.8m in pre-seed and seed funding. Norwest Ventures led, joined by Restive Ventures, Oxford Seed Fund, Collide Capital, Latitud Ventures, and Positive Ventures. beltic.com

• Elio Mortgage, an NYC-based mortgage origination platform, raised $5.1m in pre-seed funding led by Motive Partners and Social Leverage. axios.link/4rN7E2o

🏀 Brodie Rec League, a Toronto-based basketball league, raised C$5m led by Golden Ventures and Lerer Hippeau. axios.link/3TXumIw

🌍 Cotierra, a Swiss startup converting agricultural waste into biochar, raised $3m. PINC led, joined by Zürcher Kantonalbank, Carbon Drawdown Initiative, Better Ventures, GOTA Ventures, Hungry4Impact and Triple Impact Ventures. axios.link/4derc9P

• Ahron, a German HR tech startup, raised €2.2m led by Cusp Capital. axios.link/46SEg12
 
 

A MESSAGE FROM J.P. MORGAN

A banking team for the AI era
 
 

Sid Sheth, co-founder of tech company d-Matrix, knew he needed a banking team that could keep up with the demands of the rapidly evolving AI landscape. J.P. Morgan was the right choice because of its speed and scale, which helped the company expand internationally.

Private Equity Deals
 

⚡ Actis plans to invest around $2b into a new India renewable energy platform, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4xSQTnK

• Apollo completed its $3.7b take-private buyout of Nippon Sheet Glass. axios.link/4t37UcP

• Aspirity Partners agreed to acquire a majority stake in Onomondo, a Copenhagen-based IoT infrastructure and connectivity company. axios.link/4dIvXsi

🌍 CLEAResult, backed by Kohlberg, acquired CHEERS, a platform for energy code compliance registration in California. axios.link/4rC8M8G

• Hanwha Life Insurance and Centroid Investment Partners reportedly agreed to acquire South Korean financial firm Acuon Group from EQT. axios.link/4jwlkMX

⚡ Harrison Street agreed to acquire a majority stake in Vicinity Energy, a Boston-based provider of district energy solutions, from Antin Infrastructure Partners at a $2.92b enterprise value. axios.link/4hTzTc6

• H.I.G. Capital acquired Arco, a British safety equipment distributor. axios.link/4iXT7yn

• Long Lake Management completed its $6.3b take-private buyout of Amex GBT, the business travel and expense management firm. axios.link/4xTCDv6

🚑 MyEyeDr agreed to acquire the optometry division of EyeCare Partners, a Partners Group portfolio company. MyEyeDr backers include Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Industrial Investors Group, Cohesive Capital Partners, and Shumway Capital. axios.link/4hwlUrj

• Transom Capital Group agreed to acquire public safety tech company SoundThinking (Nasdaq: SSTI) for around $114m. axios.link/4rE1Nwc
 
 
Public Offerings
 

⚡ Accelevation, a Miamisburg, Ohio-based provider of power distribution and other data center infrastructure, raised $540m in its IPO. It priced at $18, below its $20-$24 range. The company was acquired last year by Olympus Partners, and plans to list on the Nasdaq (ACCV). axios.link/4yar5oc

• Calm Seas Acquisition, a SPAC led by Pilgrim Global Advisors execs, filed for a $300m IPO. axios.link/4iQp23N

• Zilch, a London-based fintech, is interviewing banks for a London IPO, per the FT. It's raised over $300m in VC funding, including at a $2b valuation in 2023. axios.link/4iXenV6
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

• Capitolis, a VC-backed fintech for banks, agreed to acquire securities lending agent eSecLending from Parthenon Capital for $200m in cash. axios.link/4iPkqLg
 
 
More M&A
 

• Ancora sweetened its offer for H.B. Fuller's (NYSE: FUL) building adhesives business to $1.4b, after a $1.2b bid was rejected. axios.link/4z53OUK

🐔 Hormel Foods (NYSE: HRL) agreed to buy Westfield, Wis.-based chicken producer Brakebush ​for $1.06b. axios.link/4AHJAlu

• Hyundai Mobis of South Korea agreed to sell its automotive lighting business to France's OPmobility (Paris: OPM) for $443.5m. axios.link/4xSm1Ue

• Specialty Program Group, a unit of VC-backed HUB International, acquired HCM Unlocked, a Miami-based managed service provider focused on HR. axios.link/4ymaP3h
 
 
Fundraising
 

• Dorm Room Fund raised $50m for its second VC fund. axios.link/4hfUxmE

⚡ EnCap Investments is raising its 13th flagship energy PE fund, per an SEC filing. Its 12th fund closed on $5.25b in 2024. encapinvestments.com

• Rising Point Capital raised $325m for its debut fund focused on lower midmarket services companies. axios.link/4dddaW1
 
 
It's Personnel
 

⚡ Ben Monaghan is leaving PJT Partners to become head of M&A at BP, effective in 2027. axios.link/4iVHCrk

• MidOcean Partners hired Kit Soo (ex-Macquarie) and Bob McLaughlin (CIFC Asset Management) as principals on its credit team, with Matthew Lal (Sculptor Capital) joining as a VP. axios.link/4jtkd0q

• Portage Point Partners named Steven Shenker as co-head of turnaround and restructuring services. axios.link/4dFXxXa

• Shinichi Takahashi joined Investindustrial as head of its Tokyo office. He previously was with Lone Star Funds. axios.link/4iRNNfZ
 
 
Final Numbers
 
Data: Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, 'Financing the AI Buildout,' Brookings Papers on Economic Activity conference draft; Chart: Axios/Emily Peck

There's a nearly $1 trillion gap between spending from the hyperscalers — Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle and SpaceX — and the revenue they've taken in from AI since 2024, Axios' Emily Peck reports.
 
 

A MESSAGE FROM J.P. MORGAN

J.P. Morgan is built to help your startup scale
 
 

Dylan Taylor, founder and CEO of Voyager Technologies, said that J.P. Morgan was the “perfect fit” for his ambitious company and its banking needs. Dylan trusted J.P. Morgan to provide critical support and guidance as Voyager scaled from startup to IPO.
